kind: multi_country_combination
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore tours through Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay feature in two extended Ada Tours itineraries through South America. Uruguay is a day trip from Buenos Aires; Chile includes Santiago and a crossing through the Atacama Desert; Bolivia offers high-altitude lagoons, the Uyuni Salt Flat and La Paz. When choosing between the 20-day and 32-day programs, consider more than the list of countries: changes in climate, elevation, border crossings and the time available at each stop.
---

## How Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay connect on our existing tours

[Uruguay](/uruguay/) lies beside the Río de la Plata, [Chile](/chile/) stretches along the Pacific side of the Andes, and [Bolivia](/bolivia/) offers entirely different landscapes: Altiplano lagoons and a vast salt flat. Travelers experience these contrasts within days: walks along the Montevideo waterfront give way to flights, desert roads and overnight stays at altitude.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include these three as **principal countries**. Both programs visit more countries. The [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) begins in Brazil, continues through Argentina and Uruguay, then Chile and Bolivia, and ends in Peru. The [32-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) follows the same main South American stages before continuing through Ecuador and Colombia. These are **not two ready-made trips restricted to Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay**.

| Program | Main difference |
|---|---|
| 20 days, 6 countries | Rio, Iguazu, Montevideo, Atacama, Uyuni and Peru |
| 32 days, 8 countries | The same key stages, followed by Ecuador and Colombia |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

To compare combinations involving fewer countries, browse [Bolivia and Chile tours](/multi-country/bolivia_chile/) or [Chile and Uruguay itineraries](/multi-country/chile_uruguay/). Each combination has its own actual program: matching country names do not imply the same transport connections.

## Uruguay: one day in Montevideo, then back to Argentina

In both larger programs, [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited **by ferry from Buenos Aires**. Travelers head to the port in the morning, cross the Río de la Plata, explore Uruguay's capital and return to Argentina in the evening. This is a sightseeing day, not a series of overnight stays on Uruguay's coast.

Three things therefore matter especially: the ferry departure time, documents for **re-entry into Argentina**, and how much time remains for the city tour. If another flight follows the excursion, the ferry schedule and airport transfer cannot be planned independently.

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) serves as the base for Montevideo. On the 20-day tour, the ferry outing falls within the Argentina stage before the flight to Santiago. On the 32-day journey, it is a separate ninth day, also followed by Chile. A multi-night stay in Uruguay would require a new individual program and recalculation of the remaining stages.

## Chile: Santiago, a flight to Calama and the beginning of the highlands

From Argentina, both routes travel to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and then via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is an important transition from a major city to a dry high-altitude landscape. San Pedro is the departure point for the following Bolivia stage by 4x4.

Chile is represented mainly by its capital and Atacama. It would therefore be a mistake to expect a full journey through Chilean Patagonia, wineries or the coast merely because Chile appears in the selection. For other regions, explore [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and discuss changing the itinerary.

Avoid overloading the evening after arrival in Calama. On the 32-day tour, the nighttime astronomy outing is **optional**, while the next day involves altitude and a long drive. First assess acclimatization and readiness for an early departure, then choose optional activities.

## Bolivia: two days by jeep through lagoons toward Uyuni

The most preparation-intensive part of this three-country selection begins at the Chile–Bolivia border. The programs include switching to 4x4 vehicles and traveling through [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), geothermal areas and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The road then continues through other high-altitude lagoons toward the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

The format matters. These are two packed days of travel with remote stops and a high-altitude overnight stay, not a short excursion from a major city. The 32-day program explicitly mentions stretches **above 4,000 meters** and the possibility of altitude sickness. Traveling by 4x4 does not eliminate the physical effects of elevation.

Uyuni's appearance varies seasonally: dry salt and mirror-like water after rain offer very different opportunities for driving and sightseeing. Before choosing a date, decide what you most want to see and check access to specific sections. Weather may require rearranging stops.

After Uyuni, both tours continue to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). The program includes exploring the city, followed by [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and an overland crossing into Peru. This sequence links nature with the history of pre-Inca civilizations, but also requires road time and another border check.

## Why these three countries cannot simply be retained without redesigning the itinerary

Uruguay is geographically far from Bolivia and Chile. On the published tours, **Argentina** bridges the distance: the Montevideo ferry excursion is part of the stay in Buenos Aires, from where travelers fly to Santiago. Beyond the Andes, the itinerary continues through Bolivia **into Peru**.

Removing Brazil, Argentina and Peru would change international flights, ferry logistics, the start and end of the journey, the acclimatization sequence and accommodation conditions. A request for "Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay only" can be developed as a separate itinerary, but the existing ready-made programs cannot be presented as already shortened trips.

When discussing a customized version, first decide whether a separate city stop in Montevideo or the nature of Atacama and the Altiplano matters more. If the salt flat is the priority, more time between San Pedro, the lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz may be preferable to sacrificing contingency days for another flight.

## Entry requirements, repeated border crossings and the ferry

Even when a nationality is eligible for a short visa-free visit, **every country on these routes must be checked separately**. Buenos Aires → Montevideo → Buenos Aires involves two border crossings, while the overland Chile → Bolivia section requires time for immigration procedures. Entry from Bolivia into Peru follows.

Requirements depend on nationality, passport type, residence status and travel date. Documents may differ for Russian passport holders, other nationalities and mixed-nationality families. Check the permitted number of entries, passport validity, connection rules, children's documents and proof of onward travel. Consult the official immigration authorities of Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and the other visited countries.

We help compile the border list in the actual travel sequence and identify where documents, tickets or additional time are needed. The border authority of each country makes the final admission decision.

## Money, baggage, insurance and weather

| Country | Local currency |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | Uruguayan peso (UYU) |
| Chile | Chilean peso (CLP) |
| Bolivia | Boliviano (BOB) |

The full six- or eight-country journey also involves other currencies. Ferry and Montevideo expenses differ from small payments during a 4x4 expedition. Before remote Bolivia sections, know what has already been paid for, which personal expenses may arise and where cash can actually be obtained. A US-dollar budget helps with comparisons but is not a universal method of payment. Check bank cards, including cards issued by foreign banks, with the issuer and destination country, and arrange a backup payment method.

Ordinary city clothes appropriate to the season are suitable for Montevideo. Atacama and the Altiplano call for warm layers, wind and sun protection, closed shoes and water. Even when coastal cities are warm, highland nights and early starts can be cold. Check carry-on and checked baggage allowances separately for every flight; discuss vehicle luggage capacity for the high-altitude stage too.

Select insurance based on the actual itinerary: cover for high-altitude areas, remote-road journeys, emergency assistance and evacuation needs checking. Anyone with chronic conditions or concerns about handling altitude should consult a doctor before buying tickets.

## Choosing between 20 and 32 days

If your goal is Montevideo, Atacama and Uyuni followed by Peru's monuments, the [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) covers those experiences without continuing north across the continent. The [32-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) retains the same type of crossing through Chile and Bolivia, then continues after Peru to Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia. Those additional days visit other countries; they do not automatically mean more time in Uruguay or around Uyuni.

Compare the number of long transfers, overnight stays at altitude, domestic flights and included services in the two offers. Prices per person in double or single accommodation and the rules for domestic flights must be taken from the specific program, not an assumed general catalog price. For an individual itinerary, Ada Tours agrees the countries, overnight stops and transfers anew.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay

### Can we buy a ready-made tour visiting only these three countries?

Both current programs in this selection also visit other South American countries. A trip confined to Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay requires a separately designed route and price.

### How much time is spent in Uruguay?

Both itineraries visit Montevideo on a one-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires, returning to Argentina. No overnight stay in Uruguay is included.

### Is the crossing from Chile into Bolivia by air or overland?

The Chile stage ends near San Pedro de Atacama. The route then crosses the border by 4x4 vehicles through high-altitude lagoons toward Uyuni.

### Is special preparation needed for Bolivia?

Yes. Consider the altitude, early starts, long drives and limited services in remote areas. Suitable insurance, warm clothes and medical consultation where appropriate are advisable.

### Are the ferry and domestic flights included?

Paid services are specified in each individual tour. The six-country itinerary separately lists the ferry and domestic flights, and the eight-country itinerary also specifies domestic flights. Read the fare, accommodation conditions and exclusions for the selected program.

## Where the adventure stages take place

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} Ada Tours itineraries combining [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) under the [“Adventure”](/interests/adventure/) interest. These are extended trips: 20 days through 6 countries or 32 days through 8. The three-country overlap must not be mistaken for a ready-made continuous itinerary visiting only those nations.

**The main adventure in these selected countries is a two-day 4x4 journey through Bolivia's highlands.** Chile provides the departure point, San Pedro de Atacama, reached after Santiago and a flight to Calama. Uruguay offers one day of historical walking in Montevideo. The sense of adventure comes from altitude, remote roads and changing desert landscapes, not from advertised climbs or long hiking trails.

| Country | Role in the journey |
|---|---|
| Chile | San Pedro, start of the crossing |
| Bolivia | 4x4 vehicles, lagoons and salt flat |
| Uruguay | City sightseeing day |

This combination suits travelers wanting to include a challenging high-altitude stage within a more varied journey, with historical cities and ordinary sightseeing as well. If the goal is sports activities in every one of the three countries, the tours do not provide a confirmed set of such experiences.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama and preparation for altitude

After a sightseeing visit to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), both programs include a flight to Calama and an overland transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stop is included **for acclimatization** before traveling into Bolivia.

San Pedro lies in the Atacama Desert. The climate and temperature differ significantly from the coastal and urban stages: dry air, sunshine and cool hours require suitable clothes. However, the programs do not include a technical climb of a Chilean volcano. Optional evening excursions in Atacama may be available, with their conditions and availability confirmed separately.

Allow a quiet period after arrival in San Pedro when choosing flights. An overloaded schedule before ascending above 4,000 meters makes the following day more difficult. The overnight stay in San Pedro matters, but it cannot guarantee full acclimatization for every traveler.

## Bolivia: two roads, numerous nature stops

The morning begins with a border crossing and a journey in 4x4 vehicles with an English-speaking guide. The first day links [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) below Licancabur Volcano, the [Salvador Dalí Desert](/bolivia/place/salvador-dali-desert/), [Polques hot springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The night is spent at an expedition-style desert hotel.

Individual stops may be short, but that does not make the day easy. Some stretches lie **more than 4,000 meters above sea level**, and the tour description explicitly mentions the risk of altitude sickness. Bring warm layers, sun and wind protection, closed shoes, water and the stamina for long drives. Anyone with chronic conditions or concerns about altitude tolerance should discuss the itinerary with a doctor beforehand.

The next day visits the Honda, Chiar Khota, [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) and Cañapa lagoons, views toward Ollagüe Volcano, the Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Red-colored water, light mineral shores and a vast salt expanse appear in turn. Conditions at the salt flat depend on the weather: a mirror effect from standing water cannot be guaranteed for a particular date.

You travel between these natural attractions by vehicle; **multi-day camping treks, mountaineering ascents and independent desert crossings are not included**. Views of Licancabur and Ollagüe do not mean climbing their summits. When deciding, consider altitude, time on the road and overnight comfort rather than the vague "difficulty" suggested by the interest category.

## Why Uruguay provides an urban contrast

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is included in both itineraries as a day trip from Buenos Aires across the Río de la Plata. After the ferry, travelers visit the capital, including the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), before returning to Argentina.

This cultural excursion offers a break from the intense sequence of impressions. **The itineraries include no separate hikes, rafting, surfing, horseback expeditions or visits to Uruguay's nature parks.** To experience adventures in Uruguay itself, the itinerary would need an addition; a city day cannot be treated as a sports stage.

The third country adds another border and transport stage. Travelers return from Uruguay to Argentina and only then continue through Chile to Bolivia. The sequence cannot be described as a direct overland Montevideo–Atacama route.

## Preparation: what genuinely shapes the experience

First is **altitude**. After the Chilean stop, travelers ascend quickly into Bolivia's highlands; fatigue is possible even without a long walk. One night of adjustment does not affect everyone equally. Consider individual medical limits, avoid demanding optional activities just before the crossing and pay attention to how you feel.

Second is **temperature and equipment**. Montevideo's city day, the Chilean desert and Bolivia's lagoons have different conditions. Layered clothing helps protect against cold high-altitude winds without overheating on drives and walks. Keep essentials accessible in the vehicle.

Third is **transport and borders**. The Santiago–Calama flight, transfer to San Pedro, crossing into Bolivia and two 4x4 days need careful coordination. Weather, roads and immigration procedures can affect timing. When booking international flights independently, do not allow zero contingency time after a remote high-altitude stage.

## Choosing between two Ada Tours itineraries

The [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) is a group trip. Alongside Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay, it visits Brazil, Argentina and Peru. Key experiences in the selected trio are the Montevideo day, arrival in San Pedro and a two-day 4x4 journey toward Uyuni.

The [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) retains the high-altitude crossing but continues beyond Peru into Ecuador and Colombia. It combines group and individual excursions. Its extra days **do not mean more time for adventures in Bolivia**: the main difference is the continuation through other countries.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

For travelers primarily interested in the highlands, consider the [Bolivia and Chile combination](/multi-country/bolivia_chile/). Other active holiday options appear in the [full multi-country adventure catalog](/multi-country/interests/adventure/). The [general Bolivia–Chile–Uruguay selection](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_uruguay/) shows the same geographic overlap without a theme restriction.

## Frequently asked questions about adventure tours

### Are volcano climbs included?

No. The confirmed program within these countries involves a 4x4 crossing, lagoons, a geyser area and a salt flat. Volcanoes are part of the landscape, but climbing them is not described.

### Can we travel without hiking experience?

The program does not require a multi-day hike: the main active section uses 4x4 vehicles. However, altitude above 4,000 meters and long roads affect well-being. Assess medical suitability before traveling.

### Is one day in Uruguay enough for a nature adventure?

On the current itineraries, the single Uruguay day is devoted to Montevideo. A separate nature or sports route would require a changed program and more time.

## Three countries, three historical stories

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) under the [“Culture and History”](/interests/culture-and-history/) theme. Both journeys also visit other South American nations: one lasts 20 days across 6 countries, while the other covers 32 days and 8 countries.

Their shared historical appeal lies in the contrasts. [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) on Bolivia's Altiplano preserves monuments of a pre-Inca civilization. In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the colonial layout of the center meets buildings from the later republican period. [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) introduces the history of a port city on the Río de la Plata.

These are different cultural traditions and different ways of traveling. In Bolivia, the archaeological stop is incorporated into the transfer to Peru. In Chile, a capital-city tour precedes the trip into the Atacama Desert. In Uruguay, the entire city stage lasts one day, including the ferry from Argentina and the return journey.

| Country | Historical focus |
|---|---|
| Bolivia | La Paz and Tiwanaku archaeological complex |
| Chile | Santiago: Plaza de Armas and La Moneda |
| Uruguay | Montevideo: Old Town and Independence Square |

For history enthusiasts, consider how much time remains at each monument after driving, flying and crossing borders. A long list of countries does not guarantee in-depth visits to all of them.

## Bolivia: La Paz and Tiwanaku's heritage

On both itineraries, Bolivia begins with an unusual nature stage: travelers cross the highlands by 4x4 through lagoons toward Uyuni. A flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) follows, with a city tour and local markets. This provides an opportunity to see how daily life in a contemporary Andean city coexists with historical traditions.

One La Paz stop is the Witches' Market, known for selling objects associated with traditional Andean beliefs. Visiting it provides insight into urban culture and crafts. However, a market walk must not be interpreted as a prepaid ceremony or a meeting with a particular keeper of traditions; no such service is promised.

The main archaeological attraction is [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), an ancient center on Bolivia's high plateau near Lake Titicaca. UNESCO recognizes it as testimony to a distinct pre-Hispanic civilization that existed long before Inca dominance in the region. Calling Tiwanaku an "Inca city" would therefore be historically incorrect.

Archaeological buildings, finely worked stone and monumental spaces offer a glimpse of the ancient state's religious and civic life. The Gate of the Sun and Kalasasaya are among the best-known features. The order of individual monuments visited depends on the excursion arrangements on site; the confirmed core stop on both journeys is Tiwanaku itself.

After the complex, the journey continues into Peru. This creates a convenient geographical link between two parts of the Andes, but culturally it is important to distinguish Tiwanaku civilization from the Inca heritage encountered later at Cusco and Machu Picchu.

## Chile: Santiago from a colonial square to the government palace

The Chilean cultural portion of both journeys focuses chiefly on a sightseeing tour of [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The city's historic center is best understood through its public spaces, architecture and changing eras.

[Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/) is one of central Santiago's main landmarks. Its cathedral, historic government buildings and everyday city life surround the square. Travelers can see the plan of a Spanish colonial city preserved within a modern capital.

Another important landmark is [La Moneda Palace](/chile/place/la-moneda-palace/). Originally constructed as a mint, it subsequently became the seat of Chilean government institutions. Its history connects late-colonial architecture with later political events. Our tours introduce central Santiago, but access to the palace's interiors cannot be promised unless expressly stated.

The city day also includes squares and monuments. After Santiago, the theme shifts: a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) prepare travelers for Bolivia's high-altitude nature program. Treating the entire Chilean stage as an archaeological expedition would be wrong; the confirmed cultural content is concentrated in the capital.

If Chilean museums, individual Atacama archaeological sites or an extended exploration of Indigenous history are your main objectives, discuss a separate program. The current tours do not include that additional historical module.

## Uruguay: one day in Montevideo and Río de la Plata history

The mechanics of the [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) visit are similar on both journeys. Early in the morning, travelers leave Buenos Aires for the port, cross the Río de la Plata and tour Uruguay's capital. The return ferry takes them back to Argentina in the evening. Neither program includes an overnight stay in Uruguay.

The main benefit is seeing a second South American city in one day and comparing it with Buenos Aires, where the excursion begins. Montevideo's historic [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), Ciudad Vieja, recalls its origins as a colonial port settlement, its defenses and its later growth into a capital.

[Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/) links the historical district with newer urban development. The excursion also includes the cathedral and the central streets. Remember that this is a one-day overview: detailed visits to every museum or a specialist historical tour of all neighborhoods are not promised.

Uruguay is particularly interesting alongside Buenos Aires. Travelers see two capitals on opposite banks of the Río de la Plata, each with its own architectural details and national history. The ferry occupies a significant portion of the day, leaving less time for unplanned stops than an overnight stay would.

## The order of the three countries

Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay are geographically far apart. The chosen itineraries do not follow a single road from “Montevideo to Santiago to Tiwanaku.” Travelers visit Uruguay from Argentina, return to Buenos Aires, then fly to Santiago, continue to Atacama and cross into Bolivia.

In Bolivia, two days are devoted to high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni before the group reaches La Paz and travels via Tiwanaku toward Peru. This order combines capital-city architecture, ancient archaeology and nature attractions, but requires several flights and lengthy overland journeys.

Do not judge the cultural content solely by days spent in a country. A single Tiwanaku stop may be the most historically important part of Bolivia's stage, while much of the other time is devoted to natural sites. In Chile, the main historic component is in Santiago; in Uruguay, it is limited to a day trip.

## Choosing between 20 and 32 days

[Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) is a group journey that visits Brazil and Argentina before Uruguay, followed by Chile, Bolivia and Peru. In the selected cultural trio it features Montevideo, a Santiago overview, La Paz and Tiwanaku. Inca history is then explored in Peru.

[Eight South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) keeps those main historical stops and continues through Ecuador and Colombia. The additional days broaden the geography and bring cultural sites in other countries; they do not mean more time exploring Montevideo, Santiago or Tiwanaku.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If your time is limited and your priorities are the historical sites listed above together with Peru, the 20-day route is the shorter overall program. If you want to continue discovering South America in Ecuador and Colombia, the extended 32-day option is appropriate.

For the same geography without a thematic filter, use the [Bolivia–Chile–Uruguay selection](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_uruguay/). You can also explore [all multi-country cultural routes](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) and [historical tours of Bolivia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/).

## Preparing for a cultural journey

Before departure, identify the historical sites you most want to see. If you dream of studying Tiwanaku in detail or spending an entire day at Santiago's museums, check how much time the current itinerary allows. The basic excursions are designed as a continuous journey through numerous countries.

Physical conditions matter too. Tiwanaku is visited in Bolivia's highlands, after road days with stretches above 4,000 meters. Interest in history does not remove the need to consider well-being and acclimatization. On city tours in Santiago and Montevideo, walking is usually the main physical activity, but ferry and air transfers also consume time.

When comparing prices, look at confirmed services on the two individual tours: domestic flights, transfers, included excursions and guiding language. Visit schedules and access to building interiors may depend on actual opening arrangements. Agree on these details before choosing a program, especially if one monument is your main reason for traveling.

## Frequently asked questions about the culture of Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay

### Is Tiwanaku part of Inca civilization?

No. Tiwanaku is the archaeological complex of a distinct pre-Inca civilization in present-day Bolivia. Travelers encounter Inca heritage later during the Peru stage.

### How much time is allocated to Uruguay?

Both itineraries include one day with a ferry from Buenos Aires and return to Argentina. The main destination is Montevideo. There are no overnight stays or separate journeys to other Uruguayan towns.

### Can we go inside La Moneda Palace?

The itinerary confirms sightseeing in Santiago and its historical areas. An interior tour of La Moneda is not specified and must not be assumed to be included.

### How does the cultural portion of the 32-day tour differ from the 20-day version?

The main stops in Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay are the same. The 32-day tour includes more countries because it continues through Ecuador and Colombia.

## Food and wine in Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay: what the current itinerary includes

**For a wine-themed trip, distinguish included services from optional activities.** We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with this geography and food-and-wine interest. The actual current option is [“Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days”](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). In addition to Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay, it visits Brazil, Argentina and Peru. It is one connected route, not a separate tour visiting only three countries.

The clearest wine experience is near [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/): after city sightseeing, travelers have the option of visiting wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) for a tasting **at extra cost**. The included portion is the capital-city tour. Uruguay offers a visit to Montevideo and Bolivia a nature-focused 4x4 journey. Separate wine tastings in these two countries are not confirmed among the tour services.

If your goal is several wineries, themed lunches and sessions with a sommelier, agree on the number of food-focused days separately. Also browse [other multi-country culinary itineraries](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) and [food-and-wine travel](/interests/food-and-wine/). Here we are discussing specifically Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay.

## Chile: one substantial wine option near Santiago

The [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) day is dedicated to downtown, Plaza de Armas, La Moneda Palace, Santa Lucía Hill and modern neighborhoods. [Maipo](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) wineries can be visited **on an optional tasting excursion**, rather than automatically as part of the package. The timing and conditions must be aligned with the city tour so one activity does not displace the other.

Why Maipo? The valley is part of central Chile's wine-producing region, relatively near the capital. An excursion can introduce winemaking and local wines while keeping Santiago as the transport base. However, the current tour does not specify the estates or the exact wines to be tasted. Selecting them for travelers based on attractive photographs would be inappropriate.

The next program stage is a flight to Calama and a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama. An extra wine day cannot simply be inserted "on the way" to Bolivia: the scheduled flight and travel time need to be considered. Compare other options in the [Chile food-and-wine tour catalog](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/).

## Uruguay: a day in Montevideo, without a confirmed wine tasting

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited from Buenos Aires. Early in the morning, participants travel to the port, cross the Río de la Plata estuary by ferry and see Montevideo's port, Independence Square, Old Town and cathedral. There is free time before the return ferry to Argentina. Ferry tickets are included in the program.

Free time can be used for an independent lunch and a taste of the city's food. **A winery, wine tasting or dedicated culinary guide is not confirmed for the Uruguay day.** Visiting Uruguay for wine would require an additional excursion outside the city and possibly another overnight stay. Combining that with a short Montevideo outing without revising the itinerary would be difficult.

The immigration arrangements also matter: a one-day visit involves leaving Argentina, entering Uruguay and crossing the border again on the same day. Requirements for multiple entries, visas and documents must be checked **for each traveler's nationality** before ferry tickets are arranged. A short journey does not remove immigration formalities. Itineraries with this geographic combination appear on the [Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_uruguay/) page.

## Bolivia: a high-altitude expedition changes food expectations

In Bolivia, the route visits [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), other high-altitude lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Travel is by 4x4, with an overnight stay in an expedition-style desert hotel. La Paz and Tiwanaku follow before the crossing into Peru. This stage is devoted to nature and discovery; its main constraints are elevation, the road and meals arranged in advance.

Parts of the route are above 4,000 meters. Rapid ascent can cause altitude sickness even in healthy travelers. On the first high-altitude days it is better to avoid alcohol tastings or heavy banquets: CDC acclimatization guidance specifically advises avoiding alcohol during the initial period. Confirm meal arrangements, drinking-water supplies and stops along the way. A packed lunch is provided on the Bolivia 4x4 stage, but a separate culinary excursion is not included.

That distinguishes this route from a wine holiday devoted to restaurants and estates. [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) have local and regional cuisines, but visits to particular restaurants cannot be assumed to be included without explicit confirmation.

## Money, food products and three different travel settings

The combination uses different national currencies: the boliviano in Bolivia, Chilean peso in Chile and Uruguayan peso in Uruguay. No universal guarantee exists for accepting US dollars or an international or Russian bank card. It is more practical to allocate funds in advance among everyday spending, optional excursions and a reserve than to rely on one payment method in all three countries.

Chile separately controls imports of plant- and animal-origin products. On flights and overland border crossings, products subject to declaration rules must be declared; the control authority decides whether entry is permitted. This is relevant to anyone buying cheese, cured meats, fruit or edible souvenirs. Uruguayan and Bolivian requirements should be checked separately, along with airline rules.

Ada Tours helps arrange the order of countries, coordinate an extra winery visit near Santiago, clarify high-altitude meals and identify passport and luggage checks in advance. Travelers whose primary interest is wine may be better served by shortening nature transfers and adding winery days rather than forcing them into an already packed schedule.

## Frequently asked questions about food experiences in Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay

### Is wine tasting included in the tour price?

No. The 20-day itinerary lists a Maipo Valley winery visit and tasting as an optional paid excursion. Other included services are specified on the [tour's own page](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/).

### Can we visit Uruguay's wineries and Montevideo in one day?

The current Uruguay day consists of a ferry trip from Buenos Aires, a city tour and a return ferry. No winery is included. More time should be discussed for a wine-focused itinerary.

### What matters more for a culinary tour: grape harvest season or the full tour dates?

If winemaking is the priority, choose the region, wineries and preferred activities first, then check available dates. The existing tour follows its own day sequence, so any additional tasting must fit without disrupting flights.

### Should we change our eating habits during the Uyuni journey?

Discuss meals and available drinking water during the high-altitude 4x4 stage in advance. Long drives, limited stops and elevations above 4,000 meters affect meals. Heavy banquets and alcohol during initial acclimatization may make travelers feel worse.

### Can we restrict the trip to Bolivia, Chile and Uruguay?

This selection currently contains an extended six-country route. A journey limited to the three named countries needs a separately agreed sequence and duration. The ready-made [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) must not be presented as a three-country trip.

## Chile, Bolivia and Uruguay: where the nature route forms a continuous journey

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both current trips — the [20-day six-country route](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) — visit [Uruguay](/uruguay/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/). But the principal **continuous nature section** links Chile and Bolivia. Uruguay is visited much earlier, as a day trip from Buenos Aires.

What connects the two neighboring Andean countries? Travelers start with acclimatization in arid [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), then cross the border and travel by 4x4 through lagoons, volcanic fields and the Uyuni Salt Flat. This is an unusual stretch of the overall journey in which the drive between natural sites becomes the primary experience for two consecutive days.

## Uruguay: Montevideo before the high-altitude section

The [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) visit follows the same pattern in both programs: an early departure from Buenos Aires, ferry across the Río de la Plata, a city tour with an English-speaking guide, free time and the return crossing. Ferry tickets are included.

Travelers see the wide estuary, the port and waterfront neighborhoods, but the program focuses on the city. Uruguay features **no separate day at a national park or natural beaches**, no overnight stay and no extended journey along its coastline. On the 20-day itinerary, the excursion falls on day eight; on the 32-day itinerary, day nine.

Nature enthusiasts should treat this brief episode as a contrast to the upcoming Andes section. Searching for a direct Montevideo–Atacama flight in the itinerary would be a mistake: travelers return to Argentina and only then fly to Santiago.

## Chile: acclimatization in San Pedro de Atacama

After Santiago, travelers fly to Calama, then drive to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This location serves as a base before Bolivia's highlands and for adjusting to conditions on the dry Andean plateau. In the day sequence, Chile has a separate Santiago city tour and a travel day to San Pedro.

Atacama is famous for desert mountain scenery, but its individual attractions should not automatically be treated as included excursions. **The Valley of the Moon, Atacama Salt Flat and Chile's high-altitude lagoons are not specified as stand-alone visits in these two itineraries.** The extended lagoon 4x4 route begins after crossing into Bolivia.

An evening telescope-based astronomy excursion in Atacama is listed as **an optional paid activity**. It depends, among other things, on the lunar calendar and confirmation. Do not confuse it with the main included nature component: the two-day journey in Bolivia.

## Bolivia: two days by jeep through high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni

From San Pedro, the group travels to the Bolivia border and sets out in 4x4 vehicles with an English-speaking guide. On the first day they visit [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/).

The natural sights follow one another quickly, but the journey remains physically demanding: high plateaus, low humidity, cold wind and long drives. Lagoon colors depend on mineral content and natural conditions; their intensity on any particular day cannot be promised.

The second day passes the Honda, Chiar Khota, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons, the Ollagüe area and the Chiguana Salt Flat before reaching [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The white salt surface creates a different impression from colorful lagoons and geyser fields. Stops at Colchani and attractions on the salt flat are also planned.

This is a **vehicle route through geographically connected locations**; a volcanic summit climb or prolonged trek is not included in the price. After Uyuni, travelers fly to La Paz and then continue toward the Peru border.

## Why preparation for altitude matters

The main practical issue is moving from coastal and urban stages into dry highlands. Acclimatization in San Pedro is included, but it does not prevent everyone from reacting to altitude. Travelers should discuss individual contraindications with a doctor and inform the organizer about limitations on long road journeys.

Warm layers, ultraviolet protection, water and shoes for short stops on rocky ground are needed even in sunshine. In Uruguay, on the other hand, ferry timing and the return to Buenos Aires matter most. There is no one set of conditions covering all these stages.

| Stage | What is actually included |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | Ferry and a city day in Montevideo |
| Chile | Santiago, flight to Calama, San Pedro and acclimatization |
| Bolivia | Two 4x4 days through lagoons, geothermal sites and Uyuni |

Both itineraries continue after Uyuni via La Paz into Peru. The [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) ends in Lima, while the [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues through Ecuador and the Galápagos Islands to Colombia. The choice involves not only price but also additional countries and overall physical demands.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Chile, Bolivia and Uruguay

### Is there a direct journey from Uruguay to Atacama?

No. After Montevideo, travelers return to Buenos Aires, then fly to Santiago and separately to Calama. Countries in the catalog describe a selection rather than consecutive stops.

### Is the astronomy excursion in the desert included?

No. The tour materials list it as a separate paid option requiring confirmation. The main included nature experience is the Bolivia route.

### Can we visit both Laguna Colorada and Uyuni?

Yes. They fall on different days of the two-day Bolivia stage. Evaluate driving and stop times from the complete schedule for the chosen tour.

### Can we take only the Chile–Bolivia portion without Uruguay?

There is no such shortened route in this selection. It would require an individually designed itinerary with new calculations for transport and accommodation. You can compare the full range in the [country combination catalog](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_uruguay/).
